name: Chromium Green
lede: Chromium green is the name of green pigments made from chromium oxide, and old catalogs also use chromium-oxide names for viridian.

sections.title: Two pigments, one name
sections.body:
The Pigment Compendium treats *oxide of chromium* as a synonym for chromium oxide, an opaque green [1]. It lists *emerald oxide of chromium* and *transparent oxide of chromium* as synonyms for [[viridian]] [2][3]. So the same word can mean the opaque oxide or the transparent viridian [1][2][3].

The swatch here is a gray-olive green, #839261, from Ridgway's color book of 1912, plate XXXII [4]. Its nearest name is Moss; compare [[cadmium-green]] and [[emerald-green]] [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this olive green in 157 of 23,531 paintings, as photographed [5]. Alfred Sisley has it in 5, and so do Claude Monet and Georges Seurat [5]. Our archive counts color matches, not pigments, so a match here does not prove a chromium pigment was used [5]. Compare [[bottle-green]] for another deep green [5]. The swatch is a screen approximation [4].
